purpose: Answer the 'could the capacity-invariance be a random quirk' challenge by locating its mechanism: does the policy ignore capacity effects it can see, or can it not see them at all?
method: Element-wise comparison of the admitted pilot cells' published per-step state arrays across all four capacity arms within each fleet seed {0,1,2}: vehicle-side arrays the policy's observation can draw on (veh_queue_ms, veh_k) versus RSU-side arrays (rsu_load, rsu_busy_ms). Read-only over hash-verified artifacts under data/vec-fresh/capacity-pilot/.

measured.note: Vehicle positions are trace-fixed by construction; V2I/V2V channel quality derives from positions; veh_done differs only as completion timing shifts (3,838-8,170 cells per pair at seed 0).

conclusion: The capacity knob changes RSU-side state pervasively (~41% of RSU-seconds) while every published vehicle-side quantity the observation could draw on is bit-identical across arms. Combined with the documented observation content (compute tier, EV flag/SoC, task type/deadline, own queues, V2I channel quality, V2V target tier - no RSU load or backlog input), the capacity-invariance is structural: the policy's observed world is identical across arms, so a deterministic policy necessarily acts identically. The invariance is an observation-space gap, not learned indifference and not randomness.
prediction: Because the observation-space design is shared by both audited actors, the baseline actor should be equally capacity-invariant on this grid. The predeclared crossover study can test this as a falsifiable prediction.
interpretation_limits: The observation vector itself is not among the published arrays; this conclusion combines identical published vehicle-side state with the documented observation content. Confirming from the evaluator's observation-builder source is the remaining code-level check (GPU-track lead).
Exploratory, owner_approved_candidate, descriptive non-causal; pilot grid scope only.
Read-only probe; nothing written to campaign directories or registries.
